status: M0: intents and reference descriptions; reference files are made in M1 by the reference tool (README.md)

conventions.assembly_check: the reference tool asserts that every primitive assembly lies inside its item's fit_box (plus its stated blend radius) and inside its frame; an assembly that does not fit fails the tool run
conventions.axes: right-handed, y up, z forward (the kart racer's frame, the same as glTF): the model's own right is -x and its left +x (draw.rs: right = [-fwd.z, 0, fwd.x]); fit_box is [length (z), width (x), height (y)] in metres
conventions.masses: sizes in the reference descriptions are written x by y by z (width by height by depth) unless a line says otherwise

views.front: orthographic, camera on +z looking towards -z (sees the nose)
views.side: orthographic, camera on +x looking towards -x (nose to the left of the image)
views.top: orthographic, camera on +y looking down, nose up in the image
views.chase: kart only: perspective from the kit's default chase camera pose (distance, height, field of view from the kit's registered camera params at the commit used), recorded with the reference

conventions.silhouette_format: 8-bit greyscale PNG mask (255 inside, 0 outside), 512 px on the frame's longest side; the frame is fixed in metres per item (frame_m, centre), never fitted to the candidate, so scale errors count
conventions.mesh_format: glTF 2.0 .glb, reference mesh as drawn (overlapping primitives), plus an outer-surface point set (outer.bin, 1 cm voxel union) for Chamfer distance and F1
conventions.frame_centre: each view's frame is frame_m metres square and fixed per item: horizontally on the centre of the reference's own bounding box (x for front and top, z for side and top), recorded in ref.json; vertically the ground (y 0) lies 5% of the frame above the bottom edge; items with stands: none (the cloud) are centred vertically on their bounding box instead. The frame is never moved to fit a candidate.
